app.title: UNIVAULT
app.description: Prototype document vault. Every document here is synthetic. No government system is connected.
banner.offlineStore: Offline demo store (no database key on this machine; resets on restart)
nav.label: Main menu
lang.label: Language
footer.issuer: The issuer is a simulation. Hashes and signatures are real cryptography; no government system is connected.
footer.attestation: Selective disclosure here is a signed attestation by UNIVAULT, not a zero-knowledge proof. Revocation cannot recall copies already downloaded. A watermark traces a leak; it cannot stop screenshots.
api.offline: You are offline. Nothing was sent and nothing was lost; try again when you are back online.
api.failed: That did not work right now. Nothing was changed.
explain.overrideDone: Saved in the history of changes. Nothing was edited.
explain.disputeDone: Your request for a review was saved in the history of changes.
ledger.title: History of changes
ledger.ok: History intact: {n} entries, every tamper-proof seal matches.
vault.title: Your vault
vault.intro: {n} documents. Originals can never be edited; corrections, links and checks are added as separate, signed layers.
vault.immutable: Tiers: a solid badge means the issuer verified it, an outlined badge means you uploaded it, a dashed badge means you corrected it.
vault.lock: the original can never be edited
vault.injectionTitle: This document contains text that looks like instructions.
vault.injectionNote: It was treated as data and ignored. Nothing in a document can share anything.
vault.notChecked: Not checked with the issuer yet.
dup.rescan: A rescan of the same paper
review.caption: Text read from this photo
review.confirmedMsg: {field} confirmed. The original reading is unchanged.
review.correctedMsg: {field} fixed. The original reading is unchanged.
readiness.title: Readiness
readiness.intro: For each purpose, every rule says pass, fail or unknown, with the reason and the documents it used. Checked on {today}.
readiness.preview: Preview what a recipient would see
names.title: Are these the same person?
names.intro: Sometimes two documents spell a name differently. We show them side by side, and you decide.
names.never: Nothing is joined unless you tap “Yes”. Your answer is saved in the history of changes.
names.none: No names to check right now.
names.others: Other pairs that are probably different people ({n})
verdict.unlikely: Unlikely to be the same person
verify.title: Check with the issuer
verify.intro: Each document with an issuer number can be checked against the issuer's signed record.
verify.simulated: The issuer is SIMULATED. Each attempt waits at most 8 seconds; if the issuer is unreachable we retry after 10, 30, 60 and 120 seconds.
verify.confirmFirst: Please confirm the text read from this scan first
verify.neutral: This copy doesn't match the issuer's record in: {fields}. This may be a scanning or typing mistake; please check it against your original.
verify.forged: The issuer's reply failed its signature check, so it was not trusted. Nothing about this document was accepted from that reply.
verify.issuerUpdate: The issuer published version {latest}. Your copy matches version {mine}. Changed: {fields}.
verify.retriesDone: Automatic tries finished. Use “Try again now”.
verify.staleBadge: Checked long ago: check again before sharing
ocr.title: Scan and fix
ocr.intro: Four sample photos of a marksheet, each damaged in a different way. Add one to your documents, then check each box.
ocr.unconfirmed: The computer can misread. Nothing counts until you say “This is correct” or fix it.
ocr.modeSaved: Saved results ({engine}, English + Telugu, run on {date}); works offline
ocr.modeLive: Run Tesseract.js now in this browser (downloads the language data the first time)
ocr.readCaption: What the computer read (not in your documents yet)
ocr.runLive: Read this scan with Tesseract now
ocr.liveFailed: Live OCR could not run here (no network?). The saved results are still available.
ocr.stored: Added to your documents. Now check each box.
ocr.evalNote: Compared field by field with the known correct text of each generated scan (the ground-truth label file). Exact match only. This panel grades results; it never makes a decision.
ocr.accuracyCaption: Field-level accuracy before and after your corrections
ocr.calibCaption: Confidence calibration (saved OCR results): when the reader was this sure, how often was it right?
ocr.calibNote: If a band's real accuracy is far below its stated confidence, that confidence should not be trusted on its own; this is why every OCR field still needs your confirmation.
assistant.title: Assistant
assistant.intro: Ask "get me ready" for a purpose. The assistant reads your vault and the rules and proposes next steps.
assistant.never: It only proposes. It cannot share, verify or change anything, and text inside documents is treated as data, never as instructions. It uses fixed rules, not an AI model.
assistant.proposalOnly: Proposal only: nothing happens until you act yourself
assistant.counts: Ledger lines before: {lb}, after: {la}. Shares before: {sb}, after: {sa}. The assistant wrote nothing and shared nothing.
card.verify_document: Check this document with the issuer
card.contact_issuer: Ask the issuer about this document
card.confirm_scan: Confirm the text read from your scan
card.review_names: Review names that look like different people
card.prepare_share_draft: Prepare a share draft (you will preview and confirm it)
faults.title: For demonstration
faults.intro: These switches pretend that something goes wrong, so you can see how UNIVAULT copes and recovers. They are only for showing the app. Every switch is saved in the history of changes.
faults.status: Now: {docs} documents, {ledger} ledger lines, {shares} shares, {registry} issuer records.
faults.issuer_timeout.title: Issuer timeout
faults.issuer_timeout.response: The simulated issuer stalls longer than the 8-second limit. Verification shows "Unverified: issuer unreachable at HH:MM, retrying" and retries automatically after 10, 30, 60 and 120 seconds. It is never shown as a mismatch.
faults.issuer_timeout.recovery: Turn the fault off; the next automatic retry (or Retry now) verifies normally.
faults.issuer_timeout.on: Issuer is now unreachable. Try Verification to see the retry behaviour.
faults.stale_data.title: Stale data
faults.stale_data.response: Every verification made before now is treated as older than 24 hours: it is labelled "stale", readiness no longer counts it as passed, and it must be re-verified before any share.
faults.stale_data.recovery: Verify the document again (a fresh check is fresh), or turn the fault off.
faults.stale_data.off: Freshness is back to the normal 24-hour rule.
faults.malformed.title: Malformed upload
faults.malformed.response: The upload is refused with a plain list of what is wrong. Nothing is stored and the problem is logged without the document's contents.
faults.malformed.recovery: Nothing to undo; upload a well-formed document.
faults.malformed.result: Refused (HTTP {status}) with {problems} reasons. Documents before: {before}, after: {after}; nothing was stored.
faults.conflicting.title: Conflicting update from the issuer
faults.conflicting.response: The simulated issuer publishes a new signed version of a record with one field changed (old versions stay). Verifying the document then shows that your copy matches the earlier version and names the changed field; any share must be re-reviewed.
faults.conflicting.recovery: Issuer records are append-only, so this cannot be switched off: get the updated document from the issuer and add it to the vault.
faults.conflicting.result: The issuer published version {v} with a changed {field}. Verify the document to see the difference.
faults.connectivity.title: Connectivity loss
faults.connectivity.response: While offline, every button refuses to send and says so; nothing is half-saved and nothing is lost.
faults.connectivity.recovery: Turn the fault off (or reconnect) and repeat the action.
faults.connectivity.on: This browser is now offline for UNIVAULT. Try any button to see the response.
faults.connectivity.off: Back online. Nothing was lost; repeat any action that was refused.
preview.title: Recipient preview
preview.heading: What a recipient for "{purpose}" would see
preview.notShared: Preview only: no share, link or code has been created.
preview.attestationNote: UNIVAULT signs this proof, and UNIVAULT sees your full data. It is not a zero-knowledge proof.
preview.watermark: The watermark traces a leak back to this recipient; it cannot stop screenshots.
preview.revocation: Revoking a share stops access, but cannot recall copies already downloaded.
preview.light: This page has no scripts, so it opens quickly on slow connections.
field.name: Name
field.author: Author
db.notConfiguredBody: This deployment has no database key, so it cannot show or store anything. Set NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY (and the four server-only signing keys) in the hosting settings, then redeploy.
share.title: Share something
share.intro: Four short steps. You will see exactly what they will see before anything is shared.
share.itemsNote: Ticked items are what this purpose needs. Anything more is flagged as over-broad.
share.viewOnly: They can only look (no file is ever sent)
share.download: They can download a stamped copy
share.previewReady: Preview ready. Check it, then confirm.
share.reverified: Checked with the issuer just now
share.blocked: A document doesn't currently match the issuer's record, or was replaced or revoked. This share can't be confirmed until you look at it.
share.overbroad: This asks for more than it needs.
share.exactly: Exactly what they will see (watermark sample)
share.confirmNote: Nothing is shared until you press “Share now”.
share.retrySafe: The connection dropped before we heard back. Nothing is lost: press Confirm again. The same request key is reused, so it cannot create a second share.
share.created: Share created for {name}. The receipt is below.
receipt.title: Your share is ready
receipt.done: Shared with {name}. Only the items below, only until the end date.
receipt.ledgerOk: written in the history of changes
receipt.codeHow: On the link page they type their recipient ID and get a fresh one-time code for each opening (works once, for 10 minutes).
receipt.once: The link is shown only now and is not stored (only its fingerprint is). Send it to the recipient yourself. This prototype sends no real SMS or email: the one-time code is shown on the recipient's screen, labelled SIMULATED.
shares.title: My shares
shares.intro: Every link you have shared, what each person can see, and until when.
shares.none: You have not shared anything yet. Tap “Share something new” to start.
shares.killed: Sharing stopped. If they already saved a copy, we cannot remove it.
shares.killedAll: {n} shares stopped. Copies already saved cannot be removed.
outcome.denied:otp_reused: Denied: that one-time code was already used.
outcome.denied:revoked: Denied: the owner stopped this share.
outcome.denied:max_views: Denied: the allowed number of opens was used up.
outcome.denied:view_only: Denied: this share is view-only; no file is served.
outcome.denied:locked: Locked: too many wrong one-time codes. Try again in 15 minutes.
outcome.locked: Locked for 15 minutes after 5 wrong codes
outcome.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Please wait a minute and try again.
outcome.error: Something went wrong. Nothing was shown.

notify.new_device: Your {purpose} share for {code} was opened from a NEW device.
notify.wrong_recipient_attempt: Someone tried your {purpose} share for {code} with a wrong recipient ID. They were denied.
notify.wrong_code_attempt: A wrong or already-used one-time code was entered on your {purpose} share for {code}. It was denied.
notify.killed_link_attempt: Someone tried your killed {purpose} link for {code}. They were denied.
notify.revoked_link_attempt: Someone tried your revoked {purpose} share for {code}. They were denied.
notify.expired_link_attempt: Someone tried your expired {purpose} share for {code}. They were denied.
notify.share_locked: Your {purpose} share for {code} was locked for 15 minutes after 5 wrong one-time codes in a row.
notify.issuer_change: The issuer changed "{title}"; {n} active share(s) use it. Please review them.
bell.label: Alerts
bell.realtime: Live updates (Supabase Realtime), plus a check every 5 seconds.
recheck.title: Has anything changed at the issuer?
recheck.intro: We ask the issuer again about every document in a link that is still shared (also every 60 seconds while this page is open, and once a day by ourselves). If the issuer replaced or cancelled a document, you are told.
recheck.none: {n} documents re-checked; no active share is affected.
recheck.affected: {n} document(s) changed at the issuer affect active shares.
leak.title: Trace a leaked copy
leak.intro: Found a screenshot of a shared page somewhere it shouldn't be? Type what you can read in its diagonal watermark (the recipient code like UV-R-1042 and/or the 6-letter session code at the end).
leak.label: Watermark text
leak.read: Read from the text: recipient code {code}, session {session}
leak.notFound: No logged opening matches this text.
ledgerPage.title: History of changes
ledgerPage.intro: Every share, check, correction and removal is written here. Each entry carries the tamper-proof seal of the one before it, so a secret change anywhere would break the chain.
ledgerPage.sqlTitle: See the database refuse an edit
ledgerPage.sqlNote: Paste this into the Supabase SQL editor. The database itself rejects the UPDATE and DELETE (a trigger), and verify_ledger() recomputes the chain.
ledgerPage.caption: Latest {n} entries (newest first)
erase.limit1: Copies a recipient already downloaded cannot be recalled.
erase.limit2: The document's fingerprint, type and event times remain in the record and the ledger; its content is deleted.
erase.limit3: Active shares that use this document are revoked first.
erase.listNote: Content deleted. Only the fingerprint, type and times remain.
gate.title: Shared documents
gate.intro: This link is for one approved recipient. Enter your recipient ID and the one-time code you were given.
gate.simulated: SIMULATED: in this prototype the code is shown on this screen; no real SMS or email is sent.
gate.codeSent: delivery (no real SMS/email): your one-time code, valid once for 10 minutes, is
gate.wrong: Those details don't match this link. The owner has been told about this attempt.
gate.deniedNote: If you think this is a mistake, ask the person who shared it with you.
view.title: Shared with you
share.withheld: Not shared because the scan's reading is not confirmed yet: {list}. Confirm them in the vault to include them.
view.for: For {name}, purpose: {purpose}. Only these items were shared.
view.verified: Checked with the issuer when shared
view.downloadNote: The copy carries a stronger watermark and its fingerprint is recorded.
view.viewOnly: View only: no file can be downloaded.
threat.title: Threat model
threat.intro: Each threat, what stops it, what does not, and the code and tests that back the claim. A test checks that every cited file exists. Details are in English.
threat.caption: {n} threats, with what stops them and what does not
threat.row.bruteForce: Guessing codes or hammering a link
policy.title: Policies
policy.intro: What UNIVAULT stores, erases and shows, in plain words. Each section names the code it was checked against. Details are in English.
policy.section.erase: What erasing deletes, and what it keeps
policy.section.watermark: What the watermark can and cannot do

signin.step2.title: Enter the code
signin.step3.title: Allow UNIVAULT to see
signin.numberHint: Demo numbers always start with 0000. Tap “Use a demo number” if you need one.
signin.err.not_demo: This prototype only accepts demo numbers that start with 0000
signin.err.bad_check: This number is not correct. Check each digit, or tap “Use a demo number”.
signin.err.wrongCode: That code is not right. You have {n} tries left.
signin.err.locked: Too many wrong codes. This number is locked for about {min} minutes. Please try again later.
signin.err.expired: That code has run out. Please ask for a new one.
signin.err.slowDown: Too many tries. Please wait a minute.
signin.err.notConfigured: Sign-in is not set up on this server yet.

signin.share.id: Your ID number, with only the last 4 digits visible
signin.recordTitle: What the simulated issuer sends back (demo record)
help.signin.title: Help: signing in
help.signin.1: Use the demo number in the box, or tap “Use a demo number” to get another.
help.signin.2: Tap “Send me a code”. The code appears on the screen: no message is sent in this demo.
help.signin.3: Type the code, read what will be shared, then tap “Allow”.
help.home.title: Help: my documents
help.home.1: Each card is one document. The coloured label tells you whether it has been checked.
help.home.2: Tap “Open” on a card to see what it says and its history.
help.home.3: The “Am I ready?” cards show what is missing for a job, scholarship or overseas check.
help.add.title: Help: adding a document
help.add.1: Choose “Take or choose a photo” if you have a paper document.
help.add.2: Or choose “Upload a file” if you already have it on your phone.
help.add.3: After adding it, check each detail and tap “This is correct”.
help.doc.title: Help: one document
help.doc.1: The left side shows what the document says.
help.doc.2: The right side shows whether the issuer confirmed it, and the history of changes.
help.doc.3: Tap “Share a part of this” to send only the details someone needs.
help.ready.title: Help: am I ready?
help.ready.1: Each box is one purpose: a job, a scholarship or an overseas check.
help.ready.2: Each line says Done, Needs you or Cannot tell, with the reason.
help.ready.3: Tap the button on a line to fix it.
help.share.title: Help: sharing
help.share.2: Steps 2 and 3: choose what to share, and for how long.
help.share.3: Step 4: check exactly what they will see, then send. “Back” is always there.
help.shares.title: Help: my shares
help.shares.1: Each card is one person you shared with.
help.shares.2: It shows what they can see and until when.
help.shares.3: Tap “Stop sharing” to close their link at once.
help.alerts.title: Help: alerts
help.alerts.1: Alerts tell you when someone opens or tries one of your links.
help.alerts.2: Each sentence says who and when.
help.alerts.3: If it looks wrong, tap “Stop this link”.
help.scan.title: Help: scan and fix
help.scan.1: The photo is shown big, with what the computer read from it.
help.scan.2: If a box is right, tap “This is correct”.
help.scan.3: If it is wrong, tap “Let me fix it” and type the right value.
help.names.title: Help: same person?
help.names.1: Two names from your documents are shown side by side.
help.names.2: Tap “Yes” if both are you, “No” if not, or “Not sure”.
help.names.3: Nothing is joined unless you tap “Yes”.
help.more.title: Help: more
help.more.2: “History of changes” shows every action, kept safe from edits.
help.more.3: “For demonstration” only shows how the app copes with problems.
help.check.title: Help: check with the issuer
help.check.1: Each document that has an issuer number can be checked.
help.check.3: If the issuer cannot be reached, we try again by ourselves.
help.history.title: Help: history of changes
help.history.1: Every action is written here, in order.
help.history.2: Each line is tied to the one before it, so a secret change would show.
help.history.3: Tap “Check the history now” to test the whole list.
help.trace.title: Help: trace a leaked copy
help.trace.1: Every shared page has faint text written across it.
help.trace.2: Type whatever you can read of that text.
help.trace.3: We show who the page was shared with.
help.assistant.title: Help: helper
help.assistant.1: Choose what you want to be ready for.
help.assistant.2: The helper suggests next steps. It cannot send or change anything.
help.assistant.3: You decide: tap a suggestion to go there.
help.faults.title: Help: for demonstration
help.faults.1: These switches pretend that something goes wrong.
help.faults.2: Turn one on and watch how the app behaves.
help.faults.3: Turn it off again to get back to normal.
help.threat.title: Help: threats and protection
help.threat.1: Each row is one thing that could go wrong.
help.threat.2: It says what stops it and what does not.
help.threat.3: The last column links to the proof in the code and tests.
help.policy.title: Help: your data
help.policy.1: This page says what is stored, and for how long.
help.policy.2: It says what is deleted when you erase a document.
help.policy.3: It says who can see what.

trail.title: What the system just did, step by step
hood.title: Under the hood (technical names)
hood.sha256.plain: A short code worked out from the whole file. Change one letter and the code changes completely.
hood.ed25519.plain: The issuer's digital stamp. Only the issuer's private key can make it; anyone can check it.
hood.salted.plain: Each field gets its own random 'salt' before its fingerprint is made, so nobody can guess a value from its fingerprint.
hood.ledger.plain: Every action is a new line that includes the fingerprint of the line before it, so an old line cannot be changed without breaking the chain.
hood.attestation.plain: UNIVAULT's signed statement about only the items you chose. It is a statement, not a zero-knowledge proof.
hood.otp.plain: A 6-digit code that works once. In this demo it is shown on screen; no SMS or email is sent.
hood.watermark.plain: The recipient's name, code, time and session are printed across the page. It traces a leaked copy; it cannot stop screenshots.
stepper.share.1.here: Pick who is asking. Their purpose decides which items are suggested.
stepper.share.1.next: You tick only the items they need.
stepper.share.2.here: Tick the items to share. Nothing else in your documents goes with them.
stepper.share.2.next: You choose how long they can look, and whether they may download a stamped copy.
stepper.share.3.here: Choose how long the link works and whether a stamped copy can be downloaded.
stepper.share.3.next: UNIVAULT re-checks each document with the issuer and shows exactly what they will see.
stepper.share.4.here: Check exactly what they will see. Nothing has been shared yet.
stepper.share.4.next: When you press the button, a link for this recipient only is made and written to the ledger.
trail.share.reverify.ok: Re-checked all {n} documents with the issuer just now: all match
trail.share.reverify.some: Re-checked {n} documents with the issuer: {ok} match
trail.share.reverify.why: A document may have been stopped or corrected since you last looked. We never share an out-of-date answer.
trail.share.attest.built: Built a signed statement with only the {n} items you chose
trail.share.attest.why: The recipient gets the answer they need, not your whole document.
trail.share.link.made: Made a link for this recipient only and stored just its fingerprint (the link is shown once, below)
trail.share.link.why: If our database leaked, the stored fingerprint could not be turned back into a working link.
trail.share.ledger.broken: The ledger chain check did not pass. Please look at the ledger page
trail.share.ledger.unknown: Ledger lines are being written; they appear on the ledger page
trail.share.ledger.why: Each line includes the fingerprint of the line before it, so the history cannot be quietly changed.
trail.share.inbox.listed: Listed in the recipient's inbox ({code}). No message is sent outside UNIVAULT
trail.share.inbox.why: The recipient sees it when they sign in. They still need their recipient ID and a one-time code to open it.
stepper.issue.1.here: Find the person. Only their masked demo ID is shown.
stepper.issue.1.next: You pick a kind of document your office is allowed to sign.
stepper.issue.2.here: Only the kinds your office is authorised for are offered.
stepper.issue.2.next: You fill a short form; the paper preview updates as you type.
stepper.issue.3.here: Fill the details. Each one is checked before you can continue.
stepper.issue.3.next: You review the paper once more before anything is signed.
stepper.issue.4.here: Read the paper. Nothing is signed until you press the button.
stepper.issue.4.next: The server signs it, records it in the registry and delivers it to the person.
trail.issue.authority.ok: Checked the authority table: your office may sign this kind of document
trail.issue.authority.why: A university cannot issue an income certificate. The table decides, not anything written in a document.
trail.issue.canon.done: Tidied the {n} values the same way every time (spacing, dates as YYYY-MM-DD)
trail.issue.canon.why: So the same fact always gives the same fingerprint, however it was typed.
trail.issue.salt.done: Made a salted fingerprint for each of the {n} fields, each with a fresh random salt
trail.issue.salt.none: No salts were added to this record
trail.issue.salt.why: Without a salt, someone could guess a value (like a year) by trying fingerprints. The salt goes to the holder only.
trail.issue.sign.done: Signed the registry entry with the issuer's Ed25519 key (the key never leaves the server)
trail.issue.sign.why: Anyone can check the stamp later; only the issuer could have made it.
trail.issue.registry.why: The registry is append-only: a later change is a new version, the old one stays.
trail.issue.deliver.done: Delivered it to the person through the normal intake (file fingerprint {fp}…)
trail.issue.deliver.why: It arrives like any other document and is not marked checked until the person checks it with you.
trail.issue.ledger.unknown: Ledger line is being written; it appears on the activity page
trail.issue.ledger.why: So the act of issuing is in the shared, tamper-evident history.
stepper.verify.1.here: UNIVAULT asks the simulated issuer about this document (it waits at most 8 seconds).
stepper.verify.1.next: You see each check that ran and its result.
stepper.verify.2.here: Each check that ran is listed below with its result.
trail.verify.input.hash: Read the stored fingerprint of the file
trail.verify.input.fields: Used the text you confirmed from the scan
trail.verify.input.why: We compare what you hold with what the issuer recorded, without sending your whole file around.
trail.verify.sig.ok: Checked the issuer's signature on its registry entry: valid
trail.verify.sig.bad: The issuer's reply did not pass the signature check, so it was not trusted
trail.verify.sig.skipped: Signature not checked: the issuer did not answer
trail.verify.sig.why: A reply without a valid issuer stamp could come from anyone.
trail.verify.fields.match: Compared each field with the issuer's record: all match
trail.verify.fields.differ: {n} field(s) differ from the issuer's record: {fields}. This may be a scanning or typing mistake
trail.verify.fields.why: One different letter is enough to show; it does not say who made the difference.
trail.verify.status.active: Asked the issuer for the current status: valid, checked {time}
trail.verify.status.revoked: Asked the issuer for the current status: stopped by the issuer, checked {time}
trail.verify.status.superseded: Asked the issuer for the current status: replaced by a corrected copy, checked {time}
trail.verify.status.retrying: The issuer did not answer in 8 s. Trying again at {time} UTC (attempt {n} of 4). You can press Retry now
trail.verify.status.noanswer: The issuer did not answer after 4 tries. Nothing is assumed; press Retry now to ask again
trail.verify.status.why: A record can be stopped or corrected after it was issued; only the issuer knows today's status.
trail.verify.fresh.stale: This answer is more than 24 hours old; check again before sharing
trail.verify.fresh.why: Old answers can be out of date.
trail.verify.ledger.line: Wrote the result to the ledger: line {seq}
trail.verify.ledger.earlier: This result was recorded in the ledger when it was checked
trail.verify.ledger.why: So you can always show when a document was checked and what the answer was.
stepper.kill.1.here: Stop one link, everything shared with one recipient, or everything.
stepper.kill.1.next: You confirm. Downloaded copies cannot be recalled.
stepper.kill.3.here: The links are stopped. The steps that ran are listed below.
trail.kill.tokens.none: No active link was left to stop
trail.kill.tokens.why: A stopped link refuses every later attempt, even with the right code.
trail.kill.ledger.lines: Wrote {n} ledger line(s), the last is line {last}
trail.kill.ledger.unknown: Ledger lines are being written; they appear on the ledger page
trail.kill.ledger.why: So the moment access ended is in the history.
trail.kill.test.denied: Tested the link just now: refused
trail.kill.test.open: Tested the link just now: it still answered ({outcome}). Please try stopping it again
trail.kill.test.notyet: Press "Test this link now" to try it yourself
trail.kill.test.why: You can see for yourself that the link no longer opens.
trail.kill.notice.done: The recipient will see a neutral notice that access ended. Copies already downloaded cannot be recalled
trail.kill.notice.why: We say plainly what stopping can and cannot do.
trail.open.link.ok: The link was found and is still active
trail.open.link.dead: The link no longer works (it was stopped, ended or is not known)
trail.open.link.why: Only links the owner made and has not stopped can be opened.
trail.open.id.ok: Your recipient ID matches the one this link was made for
trail.open.id.forwarded: This link was made for a different account; the owner has been told
trail.open.id.why: A link works only for the person it was made for, even if it is forwarded.
trail.open.code.sent: A one-time code was made (SIMULATED: shown on screen, no SMS or email)
trail.open.code.ok: The one-time code was right (SIMULATED delivery)
trail.open.code.locked: Too many wrong codes: this link is paused for 15 minutes
trail.open.code.why: A code that works once proves the person opening it is the one who asked for it just now.
trail.open.view.yes: Showing only the shared items, with your watermark
trail.open.view.why: The watermark names you on every view, so a leaked copy can be traced.
stepper.elig.1.here: The receiver asks yes/no questions (for example: at least 18 years old?).
stepper.elig.1.next: The owner can answer, answer less, or decline.
stepper.elig.2.here: Agreeing to answer lets UNIVAULT check the rules. It does not give anyone your documents.
stepper.elig.2.next: Each question gets met, not met or unknown, with the reason and the document it used.
stepper.elig.3.here: Each answer below says which rule it checked and why.
trail.elig.consent.done: The owner agreed to answer these questions
trail.elig.consent.why: Nothing is checked without the owner's yes.
trail.elig.criterion.unknown: {label}: unknown. No checked document answers this yet
trail.elig.criterion.why: Only the yes/no answer leaves the vault, never the value it was worked out from.
trail.elig.noaccess.done: No document was shared. Agreeing to answer does not give access to any document
trail.elig.noaccess.why: Answering a question and sharing a document are two different things.
trail.elig.ledger.why: So both sides can see when the question was answered.
stepper.signin.1.here: Pick who you want to be. A demo number is used; nothing real is contacted.
stepper.signin.1.next: A code is shown on screen (SIMULATED).
stepper.signin.2.here: Type the code shown on screen. In real life it would come by SMS; here it is simulated.
stepper.signin.2.next: You see the synthetic record and choose whether to continue.
stepper.signin.3.here: Check the synthetic record and agree to continue.
stepper.signin.3.next: You are signed in to your area.
trail.signin.number.done: Checked the demo number's format (12 digits, starts 0000, check digit right)
trail.signin.number.why: Only synthetic numbers are accepted, so no real Aadhaar number is ever typed here.
trail.signin.code.done: The code matched (SIMULATED: shown on screen, nothing was sent)
trail.signin.code.now: Waiting for the code shown on screen (SIMULATED)
trail.signin.code.why: This shows the real sign-in steps without contacting any real service.
trail.signin.consent.done: You agreed to continue with the synthetic record
trail.signin.consent.why: Nothing is opened without your yes.
trail.signin.in.done: Signed in: a signed, HttpOnly session cookie was set (it holds only the last 4 digits)
trail.signin.in.why: The cookie cannot be read by page scripts and cannot be edited without breaking its signature.
stepper.fix.1.here: Each value the scanner read is shown with how sure it was.
stepper.fix.1.next: You confirm it or type the right value. The original reading is kept.
trail.fix.read.sure: The scanner read {field} and was {pct}% sure
trail.fix.read.why: Low certainty means a person should look before anything relies on it.
trail.fix.change.corrected: You typed the right value for {field}
trail.fix.change.why: Your answer is what is checked with the issuer and shared.
trail.fix.kept.done: The original reading is kept unchanged; your answer is stored beside it
trail.fix.kept.why: Originals are never edited, so the history stays honest.
trail.fix.recorded.why: Every change can be seen later; nothing is overwritten.
trail.names.compared.done: Compared the two names (initials, word order, titles, Telugu and English spellings): score {score}
trail.names.compared.why: The score helps you decide; it never decides for you.
trail.names.nomerge.done: Nothing was merged. The documents stay separate; only your answer is linked
trail.names.nomerge.why: Merging by guess could mix up two people.
trail.names.recorded.done: Recorded as a new decision with a ledger line (you can change your answer later)
trail.names.recorded.why: A later answer adds a new line; the earlier one stays visible.
trail.erase.content.why: You asked for it to be erased.
trail.erase.fingerprint.kept: Kept only its fingerprint ({fp}…) so the history still adds up
trail.erase.fingerprint.why: The ledger can still prove what happened, without holding the content.
trail.erase.copies.cannot: Copies already downloaded by someone you shared with cannot be recalled
trail.erase.copies.why: We say plainly what erasing can and cannot do.
trail.erase.ledger.why: So the erasure itself is part of the history.
stepper.leak.1.here: Paste text from a copy you found (for example a screenshot's words).
stepper.leak.1.next: UNIVAULT looks for the watermark and matches it to an access.
stepper.leak.2.here: The match below says which recipient, when, and which viewing session.
trail.leak.read.done: Read the watermark from the pasted text
trail.leak.read.why: Every view prints the recipient, their code, the time and a session code across the page.
trail.leak.match.found: Matched an access by {code} at {time} UTC (session {session})
trail.leak.match.none: No watermark in this text matches an access in your shares
trail.leak.match.why: The session code is unique to one viewing, so it points to one moment.
trail.leak.limit.done: A watermark traces a leak; it cannot stop screenshots
trail.leak.limit.why: We say plainly what the watermark can and cannot do.
share.whyDisabled: Sharing is off until the document marked above has been looked at.
trail.open.details.wrong: The recipient ID or the one-time code was not right (we do not say which, to protect the link). Attempts left before a 15-minute pause: {left}
trail.open.details.why: Saying which detail was wrong would help someone guess recipient IDs.
trail.open.code.later: A one-time code comes next (SIMULATED: shown on screen)
trail.open.other.stopped: This attempt was paused (too many tries in a short time, or a problem on our side). Please try again in a minute
trail.open.other.why: Pausing fast repeated tries protects the link from guessing.
stepper.open.1.here: UNIVAULT checks that the link exists and is still active.
stepper.open.2.here: Type the recipient ID (UV-ID) the owner shared this with.
stepper.open.3.here: Type the one-time code shown on screen. In real life it would come by SMS; here it is simulated.
stepper.open.4.here: You see only the items shared with you, with your watermark.
stepper.open.1.next: If the link is not active, nothing is shown.
stepper.open.2.next: A one-time code is made for you (shown on screen).
stepper.open.3.next: If the code is right, the shared items open.
stepper.open.4.next: The owner can stop this link at any time.
elig.trailDone: Sent. The receiver sees only these answers.
stepper.erase.1.here: Erasing removes the content for good. Read what it can and cannot do.
stepper.erase.1.next: You tick that you understand, then confirm.
stepper.erase.3.here: The content is gone. The steps that ran are listed below.
stepper.names.1.here: UNIVAULT shows two names and how close they are. It never decides for you.
stepper.names.1.next: Your answer is recorded; nothing is merged.
stepper.names.2.here: Your answer is recorded below. You can change it later.
notify.document_request: {name} asked you for documents. Open Alerts to share or decline.
notify.eligibility_request: {name} asked you to answer an eligibility check. Open Alerts to answer or decline.
alert.eligibility_request: {name} asked you to answer an eligibility check at {time}. Agreeing does not share any document.
alert.document_issued: {name} issued you a new document ({type}) at {time}. Check it with the issuer before you share it.
up.step.1.here: Take a photo of your document, or choose a PDF or a photo you already have.
up.step.1.next: The text is read for you and shown as details you can fix.
up.step.2.here: Check every detail. Fix, remove or add details. Nothing is saved yet.
up.step.2.next: The details and the original file go into your vault as uploaded by you, not checked yet.
up.step.3.here: It is in your vault. Check it with the issuer before you share it.
up.limits: PDF, JPEG or PNG, up to 700 KB (photos are made smaller for you). The text is read on this device for photos and on our server for PDFs.
up.readingPdf: Reading the text in the PDF…
up.readingPhoto: Reading the text in the photo… {pct}%
up.noText: This PDF has no text to read (it may be a scan). Take a photo instead, or type the details below.
up.err.big: The file is too big (the limit is 700 KB). Take a photo instead, or save a smaller PDF.
up.err.kind: Only a PDF or a photo (JPEG or PNG) can be added.
up.err.read: The text could not be read. Try a clearer photo in good light, or type the details below.
up.err.label: Give the detail a name in English letters that is not already in the list.
up.err.none: Add at least one detail with a value.
up.noFields: No details were found automatically. Add them below (for example Name, Date of birth, Registration number).
up.newLabel: New detail name, for example Registration number
up.allText: All the text that was read
up.notChecked: It will be saved as uploaded by you and not checked yet. Only a check with the issuer can mark it verified.
up.photoTitle: Add a document from a photo
up.photoIntro: Take a clear photo of the whole document in good light. The text is read on this device; you check it before anything is saved.
up.samples: Sample scans for testing (demo data, not your documents)
signin.proof.1: Originals can't be edited or deleted
signin.proof.2: Share only what a person needs, per person
signin.proof.3: Stop sharing any time and see who looked

home2.tile.ready.line: See what you are missing for a job, scholarship or overseas check.

home2.tile.access.line: Review shares, stop sharing, trace a leaked copy.
home2.clear: All clear. Nothing needs your attention.
home2.clear.empty: Nothing to check yet. Documents you add appear here when they need a look.
home2.reason.rejected: The issuer did not accept it (stopped, or a detail differs)
home2.reason.attention: Needs a look (replaced by the issuer, or checked more than a day ago)
home2.reason.unchecked: Not checked with the issuer yet
home2.readyPick: Choose what you are getting ready for

features.verify.title: Check with the issuer
features.verify.line: Ask the (simulated) issuer whether your copy matches its signed record today.
features.names.title: Same person?
features.names.line: See whether two documents name the same person. Only you decide; nothing is merged.
features.ocr.title: Scan and fix
features.ocr.line: Take a photo of a paper document and fix what the text reader got wrong.
features.ready.title: Am I ready?
features.ready.line: See what is missing for a job, a scholarship or an overseas credential check.
features.copy.title: Verify a copy someone sent you
features.copy.line: Check a PDF that someone else gave you against the issuer's record. Not built yet.

features.link.line: Each share works only for its recipient, with a one-time code (shown on screen in this demo).
features.request.title: Requests and eligibility checks
features.request.line: A receiver such as Google asks for documents or a yes/no check; you answer, answer less, or decline.
features.watermark.title: Watermark on every view
features.watermark.line: The recipient's name, code and time are printed on the page. It traces a leak; it cannot stop screenshots.
features.stop.title: Stop sharing
features.stop.line: Stop one link, everything for one person, or everything. Copies already downloaded cannot be recalled.
features.access.title: Who has access
features.access.line: Every share, who opened it, when, and from which device.
features.leak.title: Trace a leaked copy
features.leak.line: Paste text from a copy you found; the watermark points to the person and the moment.
features.erase.title: Erase a document
features.erase.line: Remove a document's content; only its fingerprint stays so the history still adds up.
features.ledger.title: Proof of every action
features.ledger.line: Every action is a line in a hash-chained ledger that anyone can re-check.
demo.title: Demo guide
demo.purpose: The demo in six steps. Each step says who to be and opens the exact screen.
demo.switch: sign in as this role first
demo.step.issue: VIT issues a degree certificate to Mahesh
demo.step.issue.why: The issuer fills a short form and signs it; it arrives in the student's vault.
demo.step.check: Mahesh checks it with the issuer
demo.step.check.why: The issuer's signed record is compared with the copy, step by step.
demo.step.upload: Mahesh adds another document from a PDF or a photo
demo.step.upload.why: The text is read for him; he checks every detail before it is saved.
demo.step.ask: Google asks Mahesh for an eligibility check
demo.step.ask.why: A yes/no question about his documents; agreeing to answer does not share any document.
demo.step.answer: Mahesh answers (or shares only what is needed)
demo.step.answer.why: The request is in his alerts; each answer says which document it used.
demo.step.stop: Mahesh stops sharing and sees who looked
demo.step.stop.why: The link stops at once and is tested; every access is listed.
tour.title: Welcome to UNIVAULT
tour.add.line: Add your documents: from an issuer, a PDF or a photo.
tour.check.line: Check each one with its issuer, so others can trust it.
tour.share.line: Share only what a person needs, with a link for that person only.
tour.stop.line: Stop sharing any time, and see who looked.
p11.purpose.issue: Create, sign and send one official document to a person, in four steps. Only the kinds your office may sign are offered.
p11.purpose.issuerActivity: Everything your office issued, replaced or stopped, newest first.
p11.purpose.ask: Ask a person for specific items from their documents. You see only what they agree to share.
p11.purpose.requests: The requests you sent and what happened to each one.
